title: How Many Times Would The Ocean Kill You On The Way To The Bottom?

score_notes.retention: Hook contract kept: the 5 s ring empties on the word 'drops' (0:04.7), the first felt rung (ears) is at 0:28 and both meters are on screen by 0:41. The verdict curve is now a real sawtooth: YES, ?, NO (32%), YES, YES, MOSTLY, NO (58% crash), BARELY, NO (72%), YES, YES on zero cheats, with the peak declared at 86% and the twist from 88%. Rule two holds at every stamp. Second person is in 45% of sentences (was 22%) and every ladder minute is 36-60%. Spoken numbers dropped to 4.9 phrases/min (was ~10). There are turnstiles at 42% and 52%, 'picture it again' at 47%, and no spoken CTA. Held at 8: the twist is third person (27-33% you-sentences in the last 90 s), and the runtime is 9:42, close to the 10-minute ceiling.
score_notes.reference: Every alignment row was re-checked against research/corpus/explainer/<id>.md, and each row now has a real timestamp. Three rows were corrected: the third ERAS teaser payoff is 12:25 (not 12:28), the 'peak declared' citation sits on our actual peak line, and the 'and yet' reversal cites mzeN0BXR4e0 6:25 and 13:21. fGcgWaswMns is now in references: (as a devices-only reference). Zones are named aloud at their HUD boundaries (the mzeN0BXR4e0 ritual). Rung 1 is the longest unit (95 s) and the depth meter never rewinds. The ERAS mechanics are present: a strategy that gets punished, host rulings, the board, and an opening rule turned against you. Held at 8: we cite four references against the BRIEF's 2-3 (the fourth is devices only), and the ERAS-style teaser spacing is a little front-loaded (21/36/70/89% vs 37/63/77/92%).
score_notes.originality: The gate passes. VO-only check: max 0.07% shared 5-grams with any single source, longest shared run 5 words (stock phrases: 'the size of your fist', 'about as long as your', 'nobody warned you about the'). 'This is the midnight zone', a shared 5-gram with mzeN0BXR4e0, was reworded and re-measured. Fact errors fixed: Everest geometry (one Everest sunk, 2 km still below; inverted-Everest visual); the colossal squid replaced by the giant squid (the colossal is Southern Ocean only); Riftia and the off-path vents cut; the seafloor geometry fixed by sliding down the trench wall from 3.7 km; the snailfish ceiling now causes a death instead of being ignored; the bag is said to be lying on the floor, 'almost at the bottom'; the fish limit is hedged; 'cell membranes'; 'it breathes air, just like you'; 1929 Grand Banks replaced by the 2011 Japan Trench sediment flows; Hirondellea sized to the top joint of a thumb; visitors are 'fewer than fit on a bus'; 'the newest arrival', not 'made it furthest'. The DEEP hadal fact order is broken up. Held at 8: research/R5 is still empty (policy not checked against our own research), and the ladder template is shared with other backlog explainers.
score_notes.producibility: 88 shots, all generated by gen_storyboard.py from measured Kokoro word timestamps (durations.json, speed 1.0); every shot and event is a word anchor. Asset load is down from ~55 bespoke drawings to 7 kit additions (AliveMeter, DepthMeter markers, Snailfish, Amphipod, DumboOctopus, BeakedWhale, DeepFish) plus 30 static SVGs that only move as rigid layers. Stat gets numbers only; HeightChart is gone; SpeedBars only grows; Timer counts down. YOU has no face directions (poses, colour, rotate, scaleY, jitter only). There is one global depth track for the DepthMeter, Ocean and HUD; the board rows are written out; the scale shots use a shared pxPerM with YOU. The storyboard validates with zod on the Spark, and 18+8 stills were rendered and checked on the Spark. Fixed from the stills: double rule numbering, the rules card overlapping YOU, a missing CHEATS counter in s06, the Everest summit misaligned by ~80 px (SvgMarkup ignores preserveAspectRatio, so the viewBox is now square), the sub/Bus layout, and the death-1 tag overlap. Held at 7: six kit components are unbuilt and render as magenta boxes, and the 10 s gate render (s01-s02) has not run yet.

retention: Everest fact/logic: 'By now, you've sunk the full height of Mount Everest, and there are still two kilometres of water underneath you' (7:16). The visual hangs Everest upside down from the surface with its summit at YOU (s66; stills checked, summit meets the YOU dot).

Geometry: at 3:46 the current nudges the sled against the trench's west wall and it slides down the rest of the way (cross-section s37-s38, WALL layer in every later descent shot). The bait cam, grenadiers, avalanche and xenophyophores all happen on the wall. The vents, chimney landing and 'nap on the floor at 5 km' lines are cut or moved onto the wall.
Hook contradiction: the ring empties exactly on 'drops' (rate set from the measured word time); there is no second countdown.
Time to first rung 0:28 (ears), format reveal 0:05 (DepthMeter) and 0:40 (ALIVE + CHEATS); the front matter and alignment table agree.

Rule 2: deaths are NO stamps at 3:08, 5:40 and 6:58, each followed at once by a cheat. The '?' at 2:37 explicitly earns nothing ('a maybe doesn't earn a cheat'). Budget: three cheats, then the trip ends.
Middle sag: second real death at 58% (an avalanche on the wall, punishing the viewer's 'keep moving' strategy); the curve is YES, ?, NO, YES, YES, MOSTLY, NO, BARELY, NO, YES, YES.
Avalanche aside: 1929 Grand Banks replaced by a trench example, mud sliding down the Japan Trench to its floor after the 2011 earthquake (map shot s53).

Second person: 45% of sentences, 5.7% of words (stats.py method). Creature lines rewritten as you-vs-it: an eye wider than your face, tracked to your depth, a breath longer than your whole fall, the grenadiers circling you, as long as your forearm, swims up to your face, the top joint of your thumb, the size of your fist.

Numbers: 4.9 spoken number phrases/min. Depths are spoken once per rung, mostly as kilometres; elapsed time only at death 1 and the arrival. 2,992 m, 222 min, <2%/~45%, 12 cables, 6,957 m, 8,336 m, 30 trillion, 480 m/x19 and 3 in 4 are on screen only.
reference: Rule logic 1: deaths stamped NO at the cold (~3,000 m), the avalanche (~6,150 m) and the fish ceiling (~8,340 m), and 'Deaths: three' answers the promoted title 'How Many Times Would The Ocean Kill You On The Way To The Bottom?'. The HPNS beat stays '?', because a death there would assert an unproven fact; rule 2 says why it earns nothing.

Rule logic 2: the snailfish ceiling is now the weapon. You sink through the TMAO line without the chemistry and die (DEATH 3); the last cheat is the crustaceans' trick, and the last 2.6 km run on zero cheats.
Back 30%: three cheats then trip over; a final near-death on zero cheats at landing (needle slides toward NO and stops); 'it doesn't get any better than this' moved to the board at 86%.
Hook contract: drop at 0:04.7; first rung 0:28.
First rung longest: 0-1 km runs 0:28-2:03 (95 s, rung 2 is 43 s); the 701 m record is in rung 1 at 700 m; the meter never rewinds.

Pacing claims: measured 1,542 words; Kokoro speed pinned at 1.0 in the front matter after measuring 0.86 (148 wpm), 0.96 (162 wpm) and 1.0 (166 wpm) on the Spark; average sentence 11.0 words; 45% of sentences contain 'you'; 4.9 numbers/min.

Numbers with comparisons: the beaked whale is 'tracked almost exactly to your depth' and 'its longest breath on record lasted longer than your entire fall'; the octopus, fish and bag records are on screen only; the rescue depth becomes 'shallower than where you heard that sperm whale'.

Alignment table: 'peak declared' re-cited on the board line (8:23); 'aphoristic payoff' row removed; 'and yet' cites mzeN0BXR4e0 6:25/13:21 on the snailfish line; ERAS rows now carry timestamps (3:27, 5:33/5:49, 7:47-8:06, 7:15, 8:34, 8:38-9:57, 12:25, 14:45, 14:53, 15:41-15:47, 16:01); fGcgWaswMns added to references:; the twist row cites mzeN0BXR4e0 14:07 and leads with the bag.

Twist device: rule 3 is now 'no submarine... you'll be the first thing of ours to get there without one', so the bag (no cheats, no help) breaks it. Wording is 'the newest arrival at the bottom of the world is ours', not 'made it furthest'.
Zone labels: twilight (1:12, 200 m), midnight (1:43, 1 km), abyss (3:56, 4 km), hadal (5:07, 6 km) are named aloud at the HUD boundaries.
